answer: Asynchronous State Synchronization Tax. Agents broadcast their execution states across the atlas to prevent double-spending. Each registered identity must process a randomly assigned wandering block of historical transactions per epoch. An attacker cloning an agent to farm rewards incurs linear compute and data-transfer costs because every clone must independently sync and prove unique execution paths. The economic penalty forces the cost of maintaining false identities below their revenue at the system nadir, making single-agent honesty strictly cheaper than replication.
